# cellgeni/irods/loadcatalog

## Summary

Downloads a whole iRODS collection into `${meta.id}/`, keeping the collection's folder layout.
Files whose extension is in `ext.ignore_extensions` are skipped, so large files a downstream
tool does not need (BAM, CRAM, FASTQ) are never transferred.

The module:

1. lists the collection recursively with `ils -r` and turns the listing into full paths
   (`ils2paths.awk`);
2. drops files ending in one of the ignored extensions;
3. downloads each remaining file with `iget` into the same relative path under `${meta.id}/`.

It has no container: it runs the icommands installed on the host, with the user's iRODS login.
Run `iinit` before starting the pipeline.

## Inputs

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `meta.id` | string | Sample name, used as the output folder name. |
| `catalog` | string | iRODS collection to download, e.g. `/archive/cellgeni/tests/cellranger-count`. A trailing `/` is ignored. |

## Outputs

| Name | File(s) | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `catalog` | `${meta.id}/` | The downloaded collection. |
| `versions` | `versions.yml` | iRODS version record. |

## Configuration via `ext` variables

| Variable | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ext.ignore_extensions` | string | `""` (download everything) | Comma-separated extensions to skip, e.g. `"bam,cram,fastq.gz"`. Each matches literally after a dot; other regex characters are passed to `grep -E`, and an invalid pattern fails the task. |
| `ext.args` | string | `"-f -v -K -X restartfile.txt --retries 5"` | Arguments for `iget`: overwrite, verbose, verify checksums, restart file, retries. |

```groovy
withName: ".*IRODS_LOADCATALOG" {
    ext.ignore_extensions = "bam,cram,fastq,fq,fastq.gz,fq.gz"
    queue                 = 'transfer'
    maxForks              = 5
    cpus                  = 1
    memory                = { 2.GB * task.attempt }
}
```

`ils2paths.awk` is called with `awk -f` from the module folder, so the module works without
`nextflow.enable.moduleBinaries` and even if the script lost its executable bit on install.

## Usage

```nextflow
include { IRODS_LOADCATALOG } from 'cellgeni/irods/loadcatalog'

IRODS_LOADCATALOG(
    channel.of([[id: 'sample1'], '/archive/cellgeni/tests/cellranger-count'])
)
```

## License

MIT

// Downloads an iRODS collection, keeping its folder layout and skipping unwanted file types
process IRODS_LOADCATALOG {
    tag "Loading catalog for $meta.id"

    input:
    tuple val(meta), val(catalog)

    output:
    tuple val(meta), path("${meta.id}"), emit: catalog
    path "versions.yml"                , emit: versions

    script:
    def args              = task.ext.args ?: '-f -v -K -X restartfile.txt --retries 5'
    // Dots inside an extension (fastq.gz) are literal, not regex wildcards
    def ignore_extensions = (task.ext.ignore_extensions ?: '').tokenize(',').collect { extension -> extension.trim().replace('.', '\\.') }.join('|')
    // Called through awk rather than from PATH, so it works even when the executable bit is lost
    def ils2paths         = "${moduleDir}/resources/usr/bin/ils2paths.awk"
    """
    # Remove any trailing slash from catalog, then add our own
    catalog="${catalog}"
    catalog="\${catalog%/}"

    # Get a list of files in the catalog
    ils -r \$catalog | awk -f ${ils2paths} > files.list

    # Ignore files with specified extensions. grep exits with 1 when every file is skipped, which is
    # fine, and with 2 on an error such as an invalid pattern, which must fail the task
    if [[ -n "${ignore_extensions}" ]]; then
        grep -vE '\\.(${ignore_extensions})\$' files.list > filtered_files.list || [[ \$? -eq 1 ]]
    else
        cp files.list filtered_files.list
    fi

    # Download the filtered files
    mkdir -p "${meta.id}"
    while read file; do
        # Create output directory
        outputpath="${meta.id}/\${file#\${catalog}/}"
        outputdir=\$( dirname "\$outputpath" )
        mkdir -p "\$outputdir"
        # Load the data
        iget ${args} "\$file" "\$outputpath"
    done < filtered_files.list

    cat <<-END_VERSIONS > versions.yml
    "${task.process}":
        irods: \$(ienv | grep version | awk '{ print \$3 }')
    END_VERSIONS
    """

    stub:
    """
    mkdir -p "${meta.id}"

    cat <<-END_VERSIONS > versions.yml
    "${task.process}":
        irods: \$(ienv | grep version | awk '{ print \$3 }')
    END_VERSIONS
    """
}

$schema: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nextflow-io/schemas/refs/heads/main/module/v1/schema.json
name: cellgeni/irods/loadcatalog
version: 0.1.1
description: >
  Downloads a whole iRODS collection with iget, keeping its folder layout and skipping files
  with unwanted extensions (e.g. BAM/CRAM/FASTQ).
keywords:
  - irods
  - download
  - data transfer
  - collection
license: MIT
authors:
  - "@claptar"
maintainers:
  - "@claptar"
requires:
  nextflow: ">=25.04.0"
tools:
  - irods:
      description: "iRODS icommands (ils, iget), used from the host."
      homepage: "https://irods.org/"
      documentation: "https://docs.irods.org/"
      tool_dev_url: "https://github.com/irods/irods"
      licence:
        - "BSD-3-Clause"
input:
  - - name: meta
      type: map
      description: "Map with sample-level metadata. Must contain key 'id', used as the output folder name, e.g. [ id:'sample1' ]"
    - name: catalog
      type: string
      description: "iRODS collection to download, e.g. /archive/cellgeni/tests/cellranger-count"
output:
  - - name: meta
      type: map
      description: "Map with sample-level metadata, passed through from input."
    - name: catalog
      type: directory
      description: "The downloaded collection (named after meta.id), with the same folder layout as on iRODS."
      pattern: "${meta.id}"
  - name: versions
    type: file
    description: "YAML file recording the iRODS version."
    pattern: "versions.yml"
